The main takeaway from our work is that
GSH is a key determinant of DNA alkylation by ethylene dibromides, and this is the case for both in vivo and in vitro studies.

the formation of DNA S-(2-halovinylethyl)glutathione adducts is a major pathway of ethylene dibromoide-induced DNA damage and that this damage is dependent on glutathione and its conjugating ability with electrophiles.
